name: Sindang Kelingi
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Retired ISO code merged into Col [liw] 2008; no documentation of its own beyond the registration record

new_statements.quote: Dalam bahasa Sindang ciri suprasegmental yang bersifat fonemis adalah intonasi atau lagu kalimat. [...] Adapun tekanan dalam bahasa Sindang tidak bersifat fonemis. Walaupun tekanan dipidah-pindahkan [sic] posisinya pada suatu kata atau walaupun diubah-ubah letak tekanan pada suatu kalimat, maknanya tidak berubah. Biarpun demikian, bila tekanan itu diletakkan pada posisi yang tidak lazim, kata atau kalimat terasa lucu bagi penutur asli bahasa Sindang.
new_statements.translation: In Sindang the suprasegmental feature that is phonemic is intonation, or sentence melody. [...] As for stress, in Sindang it is not phonemic. Even if the stress is moved from one position to another within a word, or the placement of stress within a sentence is varied, the meaning does not change. Even so, if the stress is put in an unusual position, the word or sentence sounds funny to native speakers of Sindang.
new_statements.citation: Arifin, Siti Salamah; Tarmizi Abubakar; Hj. Kusmiarti; Hairuddin; Wowo Ario Sungkowo. 1996. Fonologi dan Morfologi Bahasa Sindang. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. ISBN 979-459-675-2.
new_statements.locator: Bab III Fonologi, sec. 3.7 'Ciri Suprasegmental', printed p. 47 (PDF p. 64 of the CORE/kemdikbud scan)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: extracted text of PDF p. 64 and the saved page image both show printed p. 47 with Tabel 9 (gugus konsonan) followed by sec. 3.7 'Ciri Suprasegmental'. The quoted passage is there word for word as printed: 'Dalam bahasa Sindang ciri suprasegmental yang bersifat fonemis adalah intonasi atau lagu kalimat.... Adapun tekanan dalam bahasa Sindang tidak bersifat fonemis. Walaupun tekanan dipidah-pindahkan posisinya pada suatu kata atau walaupun diubah-ubah letak tekanan pada suatu kalimat, maknanya tidak berubah. Biarpun demikian, bila tekanan itu diletakkan pada posisi yang tidak lazim, kata atau kalimat terasa lucu bagi penutur asli bahasa Sindang.' (the reader's '[...]' elides only the two into…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is stated to be non-contrastive: shifting it changes no meanings. The authors imply there is a customary ('lazim') stress position (deviation sounds odd) but never say where it is; only sentence intonation is treated as distinctive. No placement rule can be extracted from this source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; tempo/length (sec. 3.7, same page) likewise stated to be non-phonemic.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement covers both the word ('pada suatu kata') and the sentence ('pada suatu kalimat'); it is a phonemic-status statement, not a phonetic placement description. Data from 'bahasa Sindang' (= Col/Cul/Saling) of Musi Rawas, Rejang Lebong and Lahat, corpus drawn from one unspecified 'original' geographic dialect.
new_statements.identity_note: sind1280 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO code [sdi] 'Sindang Kelingi', merged in 2008 into Col [liw] (Glottolog coll1240, Malayic, UPPER MUSI cluster per McDowell & Anderbeck 2020). Glottolog files all Sindang descriptions under coll1240. The quoted source, Arifin et al. 1996, describes 'bahasa Sindang' (also called Saling or Cul = Col) as spoken along the Kelingi and Beliti rivers in Musi Rawas (Sumatera Selatan), Padang Ulak Tanding in Rejang Lebong (Bengkulu) and Tebing Tinggi in Lahat, explicitly including the Sindang Kelingi and Sindang Kelingi Ilir areas (sec. 2.1, pp. 6-7); the corpus was taken from one unspecified 'original' geographic dialect. Any catalog entry therefore belongs under coll1240 (Col), with sind1280 as an alias; coll1240 is itself a separate target in WORLD_TARGETS with no held files, and the three PDFs saved here serve it directly.

sources.locator: Bab III Fonologi, sec. 3.7 'Ciri Suprasegmental', printed p. 47 (PDF p. 64 of the CORE/kemdikbud scan)
sources.note: Sec. 3.7 'Ciri Suprasegmental', printed p. 47 (PDF p. 64): only sentence intonation is phonemic; stress (tekanan) is not phonemic -- it can be shifted within a word or sentence without changing meaning, though an unusual position 'sounds funny' to native speakers. No statement of where stress normally falls; transcriptions carry no stress marks. Sec. 2.1-2.2 (pp. 6-8) define the Sindang area incl. Sindang Kelingi Ilir, Sindang Beliti, Sindang Kelingi (Padang Ulak Tanding, Rejang Lebong) and Saling; language also called Saling or Cul.

sources.citation: McDowell, Jonathan & Karl Anderbeck. 2020. The Malay Lects of Southern Sumatra. JSEALS Special Publication No. 7. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. 178 pp. hdl:10524/52473 (fetched sources from CORE mirror https://core.ac.uk/download/; eVols bitstream 403 from our machine)
sources.note: Silent: the word 'stress' does not occur anywhere; ch. 5 'Phonological and morphological innovations' (pp. 56-103) is entirely segmental (*h, *s, *r, nasal deletion, high-vowel lowering, final *-a, diphthongs, *a>e, schwa, suffixes). Identity: treats Col [liw, formerly liw+sdi] as a member of the UPPER MUSI cluster of MUSI; Sindang Kelingi is a Col subdialect (not to be confused with Kelingi, a Musi Proper dialect).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request Number 2007-196: adopted merge [sdi], adopted update [liw] (2008-01-14). SIL International. 9 pp. (Glottolog ref 500783) https://iso639-3.sil.org/sites/iso639-3/files/change_requests/2007/
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Establishes identity: Sindang Kelingi is another name for / a dialect of Col; the government literature (Arifin et al. 1996, p. 7) calls the language 'Sindang' with dialects Sindang Kelingi Ilir, Sindang Kelingi, Sindang Beliti, Saling.
